verdict.rationale: LaunchDarkly's docs say SDK-passed context attributes can be used in flag targeting, and that targeting rules can also target individuals and segments. They also cover converting rules into segments. Community users independently confirm the ordered, AND-condition rule system, attribute-based rollouts and Big Segments. Missing for 10: segment documentation appears only as titles, with no explicit description of reusing one segment across multiple flags.

support.subject: As a developer, I can target flags with attribute-based rules and reusable segments so the right users see the right variation

citations.quote: LaunchDarkly SDKs can pass any context attributes you want to LaunchDarkly, where you can then use those attributes in flag targeting.
In addition to targeting specific context attributes, you can target individuals, segments, or specific mobile apps and devices.
Targeting rules are the mechanism for expressing precedence and conditions across multiple context kinds.
LD's rule system (ordered rules with ANDed conditions over arbitrary contexts) is arguably better than their internal expression language.
